_meta.purpose: Step 12, #139 — proves the null_ordering check in src/nl2sql/pipeline/soundness.py. A NULL sorts before all values, so an ascending-order / min(f) result over an unguarded column can be silently NULL-driven and wrong. Flagged as a correction signal (not a hard reject).
_meta.format: (candidate SQL, expected verdict) pairs. expected_verdict is 'flag' (soundness hit → feed back) or 'pass' (clean). Cases with expected_verdict='flag' form the catch-rate set; 'pass' cases form the false-positive set (a flag on one is a false positive).
_meta.rule: Only the OUTERMOST query is judged (the result the user receives); a scalar MIN(x) building-block subquery is a common, correct idiom and is not flagged. MAX/DESC are safe (NULLs sort last). A column already constrained by IS NOT NULL or any comparison/range/IN predicate in WHERE is not flagged.

cases.description: min(price) with no NOT NULL guard — the minimum can be driven by a NULL semantics gap; the paper's null-ordering hazard.
min(price) per group, still unguarded — grouping does not neutralize the hazard on the min column.
cases.sql: SELECT category, MIN(price) FROM products GROUP BY category

cases.description: ORDER BY score ASC LIMIT 1 to take the smallest — a NULL sorts first, so the top row can be NULL-driven and wrong.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY score ASC LIMIT 1

cases.description: ASC is the default when unspecified; ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 5 is the same hazard as an explicit ASC.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM events ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 5

cases.description: min(price) WITH an explicit price IS NOT NULL guard — the near-miss negative; must NOT be flagged.
cases.sql: SELECT MIN(price) FROM products WHERE price IS NOT NULL

cases.description: price > 0 already excludes NULLs via three-valued logic — the min column is guarded; not flagged.
cases.sql: SELECT MIN(price) FROM products WHERE price > 0

cases.description: Descending order puts NULLs last, so the top row is never NULL-driven — not a hazard.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 1

cases.description: A full ordered list (no LIMIT) returns every row — NULLs sorting first does not corrupt a result nobody truncates.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY score ASC

cases.description: MAX ignores NULLs and NULLs sort last, so the maximum is never NULL-driven — the check must not fire on max.
A scalar MIN(price) building-block subquery is a common, correct idiom; only the outermost result is judged, so the nested min is not flagged.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price = (SELECT MIN(price) FROM products WHERE price IS NOT NULL)
